messages:
eli: Heads-up — Emerald (int4) canary is showing an uptick in structured output / funcall parse failures for the web_search tool. sample: 5k requests, parse_fail rate jumped 0.9% -> 4.7% after int4 roll (cohort B). logs + examples incoming :eyes:
sasha: link to the canary dashboard? can we see which prompts fail most?
eli: https://grafana.redwood/emerald-canary -> query `funcall_parse_fail_rate{model=\"emerald-int4\"}`. top n failing routes: /agent/web_search, /agent/summarize. allocating a few example outputs below.
eli: ```
{"tool":"web_search","args": {"q": "redwood inference intro"}}}

{"tool": "web_search", "args": {"q": "redwood inference intro"},}

{"tool": "web_search", "args": "q=redwood inference intro"}...EXTRA_TEXT
```
ben: whoa those look like trailing-comma and suffix garbage cases. could be tokenization alignment after quant. did we change eos handling in the int4 kernel?
priya: tagging @ben for a reproducer. ben, can you run a small batch with the same tokenizer + int8 vs int4 and dump token IDs around the boundary? also check KV prefix truncation on streaming.
ben: running now. command: `python -m rl_onboard.playground --model emerald --quant int4 --seed 42 --route /agent/web_search --n 2000 --dump-tokens`
canary-bot: ALERT: Emerald-canary cohort B threshold breached (parse_fail_rate 4.7% > threshold 2.0%). Incident created: INC-2026-834.
ravi: fwiw we saw similar pattern last quarter where prefix caching + aggressive batching produced suffix interleaving on int4. quick mitigation: disable prefix caching for the canary or lower batch size to 1 for streaming.
sasha: any correlation with temperature or top_p? maybe sampling noise increases malformed JSON.
eli: checked temperature distribution — unchanged. failures cluster on longer tool args (q length > 120 tokens) and when summarization prompt includes code blocks.
priya: two parallel levers: 1) post-process: tolerant JSON healer to attempt fix (strip trailing commas, remove non-json suffix) 2) root cause: kernel/token alignment in int4 path. we should enable (1) for canary immediate and schedule (2) longer fix.
ben: quick patch for healer I can push to prod-route as a canary postprocess: `if parse_error: attempt regex strip trailing commas and trailing non-brace content; reparse up to 2 retries` — will add metric for healer success rate.
eli: please also add a label when healer modifies output so we can measure behavioral delta. want to ensure heuristic doesn't mask semantic regressions.
priya: agreed. also run structured-eval suite (golden prompts) against emerald-int8 vs int4 to measure fidelity drop; include function-calling conformance metrics (schema-strict pass/fail). I'll queue 10k examples.
ben: quick reproduction results: int8 parse_fail_rate 0.8%, int4 4.6% for same seed/batch. token diff around EOS: int4 often inserts a 502 (non-printable) token sequence at end -> leads to suffix. sending dump to #eng-infra for kernel triage.
ravi: can you try `disable_kvcache=True` + `batch_size=1` on the same run? that was the cheap fix we used before.
ben: did that: int4 with kv disabled -> parse_fail 1.1%. looks like KV cache interaction indeed.
sasha: good signal. priorities: (A) enable healer and metadata label for canary, (B) disable kvcache for emerald-int4 cohort, (C) follow up kernel triage ticket.
eli: agreed. I'll pause further emerald-int4 rollout and leave traffic on emerald-int8 mirror. canary patch plan: healer on for cohort B, kvcache disabled for cohort B, add heal-label and healer_metrics, run structured-eval job.
priya: assigning tasks: ben -> push healer canary + label + metric. ravi -> change canary config to disable kvcache. sasha -> run structured-eval comparison for schema conformance. eli -> open kernel triage ticket with token dumps.
eli: done. created ticket ONB-942: "emerald-int4 kvcache/token alignment triage" and linked dumps.
ben: pushed healer code to canary branch and added metric `healer_applied_count` + `healer_success_rate`.
canary-bot: NOTE: healer patch deployed to cohort B at 1789992508. Monitoring metrics.
sasha: initial healer impact (first 1200 reqs): parse_fail raw -> 4.6%, after healer success -> 2.0% (healer corrected ~55% of failures). still higher than int8 baseline but reduced.
priya: that's acceptable short-term. let's keep healer on but don't auto-merge to stable until kernel fix validated. schedule a canary window for 24h.
eli: thanks all — will sync in tomorrow stand with a short postmortem and next steps.
priya: ping me once structured-eval completes, I'll draft the regression note for release notes.
eli: 👍 thanks :filter:
